display.purpose: The one page headline. 1.875rem, stepping to 2.25rem at sm.

code.purpose: The invite code, and only the invite code. Marker red at 0.36em tracking so six characters survive being read aloud across a room.

card-name.purpose: The name written on a card — the thing that occupies a slot. Never a label about the thing.

body.purpose: Sentences. Tabular figures inherited from body.

body-small.purpose: The line under a heading, an empty-state sentence, a correction's message.

slot-label.purpose: The board's own small caps and the system's workhorse: column heads, section headings, statuses, counts, slot numbers, rail links. Shipped as the slot-label utility.

field-label.purpose: An input's label. Differs from a section heading downward — same ink, lighter weight, tighter tracking — never by contrast.

motion.name: card-lands
motion.purpose: A card landing in its slot: opacity 0 and translateY(-0.375rem) to rest. Plays only on the row that genuinely just arrived, keyed off the ?arrived=1 that the create and join actions set.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Guarded inside the card-lands utility itself, not at each call site, so a new caller cannot forget. The state change still lands; only the travel is dropped.

motion.name: transition-colors
motion.purpose: Hover and focus colour changes on interactive elements. Not animation; permitted everywhere interactive.

containers.name: sheet
containers.purpose: max-w-3xl. Every surface's measure, shared by the top rail's inner row so the wordmark aligns with the first slot below it.

narrative.overview:
The world is the physical draft board seen up close: card stock slotted into ruled slots, names written in marker, the slot on the clock struck in red. The value relationship of the real object is inverted on purpose — the card stock is the ground and the board's ruling is the ink. Draft night is a lit room with a TV on, followed by months of daylight phone checks; and a near-black surface with one glowing accent is the first thing this category reaches for, so it is the first thing this board refuses.

The personality is an instrument, not an entertainment product: cool, dry, dense where density is honest and quiet everywhere else. Nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing is rounded. Depth comes from rule weight and one deeper stock used inside framed Banks. Colour is restrained to tinted neutrals plus one marker red, and the red is load-bearing — it marks who is on the clock and what just landed, and it is never decoration.

The direction contract permits one level of programme-like task grouping: a framed Bank cut from deeper stock. It never nests, rounds or floats, so no cards-inside-cards stack can form.
keyCharacteristics: Card stock as the ground, the board's ruling as the ink; light, not dark.
One accent — the commissioner's marker red — with two jobs and no third.
State is carried by a row's own material (border weight and style), never by a pill parked beside an otherwise normal row.
Zero corner radius, zero shadows, zero gradients, anywhere.
One type family (Archivo), caps for names and labels, tabular figures for every number in the app.
Exactly two animations are implemented, on exactly two state-change events.
Mobile-first with a single breakpoint; the phone gets the complete rail.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Marker red has exactly two jobs: state — the slot on the clock and the row that just landed — and the one act — the single primary action on a surface, plus the focus and caret affordances that belong to acting. It never decorates, never fills a large area, and never appears twice as a primary action on one screen. Creating a league carries the marker; joining one does not.

rules.name: The 2px Marker Rule
rules.body: The double-weight marker rule (slot-live) means one thing and one thing only: this slot is on the clock. Marker red as text is permitted for the one thing a commissioner reads out (the invite code is written in marker), but the code's own slot stays slot-filled — ruled, not struck.

rules.name: The Correction-in-Ink Rule
rules.body: Errors are struck in ink at 2px (slot-correction), never in marker. An earlier version borrowed the marker for failures, which made an error and an invite code render identically.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Blush Rule
rules.body: Text on a live field is ink (12.62:1 on live-sunk). Marker red now clears the floor there, but ink remains the label: the marker's two jobs are semantic, not merely a contrast workaround.

rules.name: The Letter-Always Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries position on its own. A PositionPatch always renders its G / F / C letter, for colour-blind readers and for a photocopied sheet (PRODUCT.md, Accessibility & Inclusion).

rules.name: The One Label Maker Rule
rules.body: One family, no exceptions. There is no display face, no serif, no mono. Numbers are already tabular, so a mono face has no job here.

rules.name: The latin-ext Rule
rules.body: The latin-ext subset is not optional. This league reads names like Valančiūnas and Motiejūnas; a font that falls back mid-word for the diacritics makes the board look broken. Any future family must ship latin-ext.

rules.name: The Tracking-Inverts-Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking rises as size falls: 0.04em at display, 0.06em on a card name, 0.14em on a slot label. Caps at small sizes are only legible when they are opened up.

rules.name: The Computed-Family Rule
rules.body: tests/e2e/design.spec.ts asserts the computed font-family on body contains "Archivo" and does not contain "Arial". A hardcoded stack on body once overrode the token, so the webfont downloaded on every cold load while the page rendered in Arial. Assert the computed value, not the token.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: New surfaces use Sheet. If a future surface needs to be wider than 48rem (a real draft board with 12 columns will), that is a deliberate new container with its own justification — not a per-page max-w override.

rules.name: The Slot Grid Rule
rules.body: Anything vertical is a multiple of the slot unit (2.75rem) or of Tailwind's 0.25rem step. Do not introduce a third spacing system.

rules.name: The Panel Rule
rules.body: A Bank may be framed: deep stock, one 1px strong rule, zero radius and zero shadow. A framed Bank is one level of task grouping and never sits inside another framed Bank. Rows and controls inside it keep their own material; they do not become cards.

rules.name: The Flatness-Is-Not-Negotiable Rule
rules.body: A shadow, a gradient, a glow or a rounded corner arriving anywhere in this system is a regression, not a variant. The board is a physical object photographed head-on in flat light.

rules.name: The Material-Carries-State Rule
rules.body: A slot's state is its own top border. Never add a coloured pill, chip or badge beside an otherwise normal row to say "waiting" or "on the clock". This system has no chip component and does not want one.

rules.name: The Board-Shows-Its-Shape Rule
rules.body: A list of things that occupy slots renders its empty slots too. A lobby that is a quarter full looks a quarter full; the signed-in home continues past your leagues into free slots. A list that just stops is not a board.

rules.name: The Pending-Label Rule
rules.body: Every SubmitButton gets a pendingLabel written in the domain's words. "Loading" is not one of the domain's words.

rules.name: The Two Events Rule
rules.body: Nothing else animates. Colour transitions on hover (transition-colors) are not animation and are permitted on interactive elements. A spinner, a skeleton, a page transition, a parallax or an entrance animation on a static element is out of scope for this world.

dos: Do carry state in the row's own material. A new state means a new rule weight or style, defined as a @utility in globals.css next to slot-waiting / slot-filled / slot-live / slot-correction.
Do put every colour in globals.css in OKLCH and add it to src/app/tokens.test.ts. Text and patch colours clear 4.5:1 on stock and stock-deep; meaningful non-text boundaries clear 3:1.
Do give any new interactive element a 44px minimum target on both axes (min-h-11 min-w-11) and a focus-visible 2px marker outline at 2px offset.
Do render empty slots. Show the shape of the board, not the length of the list.
Do use CONTEXT.md's words. A slot is a position on the board. An earlier draft of board.tsx invented "bay" and led a page headline with it — which is exactly the drift CONTEXT.md exists to prevent.
Do guard prefers-reduced-motion inside the animation utility itself, not at each call site, so a new caller cannot forget.
Do write a pendingLabel for every submit, and a finished-sentence message for every failure.
Do use arbitrary properties for per-side border styles — e.g. [border-bottom-style:solid].
donts: Don't add a corner radius, a shadow, a gradient, a blur or any surface colour beyond stock and stock-deep. A framed Bank never nests inside another.
Don't put a second marker-red primary action on one surface, and don't use marker red for anything that is not state or the one act.
Don't strike an error in marker. Corrections are ink (slot-correction) — an error and an invite code must never look alike.
Don't put marker-red text on the live tint. It clears contrast, but ink is 12.62:1 and marker text would still violate the Two Jobs Rule.
Don't encode position or status by colour alone. The G / F / C letter is always present.
Don't hide the season from the top rail on small screens. If the rail must contract, drop the user's name.
Don't introduce a second font family, an icon package or an icon font.
Don't write border-b-solid. It is not a Tailwind v4 utility and compiles to nothing — the border silently stays dashed and the screenshot looks plausible. Use an arbitrary property.

Don't ship a system-level comment as JSX ({/* … */}). A JSX comment is a JavaScript comment: it reaches a sourcemap and nothing else, so it is a contract nobody can audit. React has no comment node, so the direction contract in layout.tsx is emitted through dangerouslySetInnerHTML and guarded by tests/e2e/design.spec.ts.
Don't animate anything new. Both events in the motion budget are built.
openQuestions: No dark mode. color-scheme: light is declared and the light ground is a deliberate inversion argued from a lit room and daylight phone use.
Input error and disabled states are unstyled; Correction carries every failure today.
A few type values are one-offs, not tokens: sm:text-[1.0625rem], tracking-[0.32em], tracking-[0.36em].
